why: A generator script and a regex codemod do the work, and the type check catches a wrong area name or a missing argument. The by-hand cases (twelve English defaults, the EDITOR_AREAS and PLATFORM_SITE_AREAS lists) are named with file and line. It still rewrites about 600 files over a dozen commits and depends on step 0.7's module shape, which this brief can only guess ('copy what 0.7 wrote'). Turning an English default into a required prop invites a caller fix that passes English words again, which shows English to Norwegian owners. Only the fallback spec would catch that.
harm_if_wrong: Norwegian accounts would see English words on screens whose default was replaced wrongly. A module value-imported into a client file would ship both catalogues to the browser if the scan's widened rule is miswritten.
make_it_cheaper: Write out the exact replacement call for each of the twelve English-default sites (which words the page passes, from which variable), as the brief does for offline/page.tsx.
brief_problems: Commit 1 says to copy the shape 'token for token' from step 0.7's modules, but 0.7's AreaWords and areaText are not in the repo yet, so the generator's output is guessed (stop_if covers a mismatch).
